rulings.R7: Tier-4 single-call arms run on the owner's ratified provider pins: the tier3_arm_a and tier3_arm_d entries of OPENROUTER_PROVIDER_ORDER. Every unit records the provider that served each call. A unit served by any other provider is recorded serving_mismatch, kept in the record and not read as a result.
rulings.R8: Tier-4 single-call arms (A, D, D-pages) run with max_tokens 32768, the cap the pipeline's implement call already has. Per-unit ceilings: A $0.15; D and D-pages $0.40. A unit whose answer ends on 'length' is recorded truncated, flagged on the reading sheet and not read as a result.
rulings.R9: Each frozen batch registers itself in its manifest.json: the sha256 of its candidates and of each F2 question's corpus pages, its families, its calibration and pilot ceilings, its per-unit ceilings, deadline and single-call max_tokens. The runner reads them from the manifest.

execution.R7: evals/tier4/runner.py maps the owner's provider-order line: _map_tier4_pins drops any existing tier4_arm_a/tier4_arm_d entries (the mapping is idempotent over its own output) and appends tier4_arm_a:<the line's tier3_arm_a> and tier4_arm_d:<the line's tier3_arm_d>. A tier3 entry with no provider maps to an explicitly empty tier-4 entry — unpinned, and refused — because an absent key would fall to the line's general list, which is what served the void calibration. tier4_pins(line) installs the mapped line on the harness settings singleton for the run's duration and restores it afterwards; the routing layer reads the singleton per call, so every single-call arm's chat carries its pin's provider order. _arm_pin_key(arm) is tier4_arm_<ceiling_key(arm)> (D-pages bills to tier4_arm_d); _arm_pin(arm) resolves it through provider_order_for, where an empty-value tier entry resolves to an empty list — an empty pin is a refusal, never a fall to the general list. The preflight prints each single-call arm's pin ('arm A: pinned to … (R7: the owner's ratified tier3_arm_a pin, re-keyed to the tier-4 function the arm bills to)') and each pipeline arm's per-tier provider order, and refuses to start an arm with no pin, naming the tier4_arm_a/tier4_arm_d key the line registers no entry for. Every unit's record carries providers_by_tier — the provider that actually served each call.
execution.R8: evals/tier3/runner.py's _registered_call and _arm_single take an additive max_tokens parameter defaulting to the registered cap (the tier-3 behaviour is unchanged unless a caller passes its own); the tier-4 executor passes the batch's registered single_call_max_tokens (32768) for the single-call arms. UnitResult.truncated is set when any finish_reason is 'length', and tier4_unit_record carries it into the record; the reading sheet flags it and the readable counts exclude flagged units. The per-unit ceilings (A $0.15, D and D-pages $0.40, F $0.40, E $1.50), the deadline (3600 s) and the single-call max_tokens are the batch's own registrations, read from its manifest, and the preflight computes every single-call worst case at the registered cap.
execution.R9: Every frozen batch registers itself in its manifest.json and the runner reads it (Tier4Batch, load_batch, --batch DIR on every subcommand; the default is the pilot batch). The manifest carries the candidates path and sha256, each question's corpus pages with the sha256 over the listed pages concatenated in the listed order, the families, the calibration and pilot ceilings, the per-unit ceilings, the deadline and the single-call max_tokens. The freeze guard (check_freeze) hashes the candidates file and each question's pages against the manifest's registrations and refuses a mode naming the question and the pages that drifted; a one-byte change to batch 2's candidates or either corpus page refuses. The calibration plan comes from the batch — every F1 question x A and D, every F2 question x D-pages, one repetition — so batch 2 plans exactly its two D-pages units (T4-15, T4-16) at its registered $1.00 ceiling, and the pilot batch still plans its nine. Every F2 unit of arms F and E grounds with its own question's pages and no other's: a question whose pages are the tier-4 profile's own corpus pages (the pilot batch's T4-06) runs under the shipped tier4 profile, any other F2 question runs under a per-question profile whose scratch manifest lists that question's frozen pages only; D-pages carries its own question's pages under the registered separator. The gate stays exact against the manifest's registered ceiling ($2.00 pilot-batch calibration, $1.00 batch-2 calibration, $5.00 pilot). evals/tier4/pilot/ gets a manifest in the same format with its candidates and corpus byte-identical to the freeze, so the pilot batch runs exactly as before.
